name: BIND 9
author: Netlens
description: Registers your devices in a BIND 9 (or any RFC 2136 compatible) DNS server: an A record and a reverse (PTR) record for every device Netlens knows and DNS does not, and a changed address for devices whose IP changed (DHCP). Reads zones by zone transfer (AXFR) and writes by dynamic update (RFC 2136), both signed with a TSIG key. Every change is guarded by a prerequisite, so a record that changed meanwhile is never overwritten. Netlens only changes records it remembers writing.

info.title: Allow Netlens in named.conf
info.text: Make a TSIG key (tsig-keygen netlens-key), add it to named.conf, and allow it to transfer and update your zones. The zones must be dynamic: BIND then keeps a journal next to the zone file and the directory must be writable by named. Reload with rndc reload.

config.label: BIND servers
config.help: The primary server that holds the zones (secondaries get the change by zone transfer and must not be listed).

columns.label: Server address
columns.help: An address, optionally with a port: 192.168.0.2:5353

config.label: Reverse zones
config.help: Comma separated. DNS cannot list zones, so name the reverse zones Netlens should keep up to date (the forward zones come from the DNS registration page).

config.label: TTL for new records (seconds)
config.help: A dynamic update must carry a TTL.
